briefing: Eleven brothers set out for home from Egypt with full sacks of corn, and a costly silver cup goes missing from the house of the ruler. Your case file is Genesis 44: trace how the cup got into the sack, how it was found, and how the matter was settled.

stages.clue: Household record: before dawn, the master of the house gave private orders about the travellers' sacks, including special instructions about his own cup.
stages.prompt: According to the text, who ordered the silver cup to be put in the youngest brother's sack?
options: Joseph, who commanded his steward to do it
Benjamin, who hid it there himself
Judah, who wanted to test his brothers
Reuben, who took it from the table
stages.explanation: Joseph commanded his steward to put 'my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest,' and the steward 'did according to the word that Joseph had spoken' (Genesis 44:1-2).
stages.hint: Read who 'commanded the steward of his house.'

stages.clue: Witness statement: 'They were out of the city but not yet far off when the steward caught up with us and asked us a hard question.'
stages.prompt: What question did Joseph tell the steward to put to the men when he overtook them?
options: Wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?
Why have ye not paid for your corn?
Where is your youngest brother?
Why did ye leave before morning?
stages.explanation: Joseph instructed the steward to say, 'Wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?' and to describe the cup as the one in which his lord drinks and divines (Genesis 44:4-5).
stages.hint: The question contrasts two opposites: what they received and what they gave back.

stages.clue: Transcript of the roadside exchange: the brothers, sure of their innocence, proposed a severe penalty, but the steward set his own terms.
stages.prompt: What terms did the steward state for the one with whom the cup was found?
options: He shall be my servant; and the rest shall be blameless
All the brothers shall be put to death
He shall pay back the cup's value twice over
He shall be sent home in disgrace
stages.explanation: The brothers offered death for the guilty one and bondage for themselves, but the steward said, 'he with whom it is found shall be my servant; and ye shall be blameless' (Genesis 44:9-10).
stages.hint: The steward's terms were narrower than the brothers' own offer.

stages.clue: Search report: each sack was lowered to the ground and opened, beginning with the eldest brother and ending with the youngest.
stages.prompt: Where was the cup found, and what did the brothers do next?
options: In Benjamin's sack; they rent their clothes and returned to the city
In Judah's sack; they fled toward Canaan
In Reuben's sack; they hid it again
In Simeon's sack; they left him behind
stages.explanation: The steward 'began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack'; then the brothers 'rent their clothes' and returned to the city (Genesis 44:12-13).
stages.hint: The search ended with the youngest brother.

stages.clue: Final statement before the ruler: one brother stepped forward, explaining that he had pledged himself to his father for the lad's safe return.
stages.prompt: How did Judah propose to resolve the case?
options: He asked to remain as a bondman instead of the lad, so the lad could go home
He offered to pay double silver for the cup
He accused the steward of planting the cup
He asked that all the brothers stay in Egypt except Judah
stages.explanation: Judah said he 'became surety for the lad unto my father' and asked to 'abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren' (Genesis 44:32-33).
stages.hint: Judah had made himself responsible for the youngest before his father.

batch.title: The Silver Cup in the Sack

briefing: Samson, the judge of Israel, has broken every bond his enemies placed on him, and no one knows why he cannot be overpowered. In Judges 16 a woman is offered a fortune to uncover his secret. Your task is to follow the evidence, stage by stage, to learn how the strongest man in Israel was finally brought low.

stages.clue: Case note: The file opens after Samson's escape from Gaza. Our informant says he has come to love a woman who lives in a certain valley.
stages.prompt: According to the text, where did Delilah live?
options: In the valley of Sorek
In the city of Gaza
In the house of Dagon
In the town of Zorah
stages.explanation: Judges 16:4 says Samson loved a woman "in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah."
stages.hint: The location is named in the same verse that first names Delilah.

stages.clue: Intercepted message: Powerful men came up to Delilah's house with a proposal and a price for her cooperation.
stages.prompt: Who approached Delilah, and what did each of them promise her?
options: The priests of Dagon, each promising a talent of gold
The lords of the Philistines, each promising eleven hundred pieces of silver
Samson's father and mother, each promising a flock of sheep
The men of Judah, each promising thirty changes of garments
stages.explanation: In Judges 16:5 the lords of the Philistines asked Delilah to entice Samson and promised, "every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver."
stages.hint: The offer was made in silver, and it came from Israel's enemies.

stages.clue: Evidence bag #1: Fresh, pliable cords found near the room, with Philistines reported lying in wait. Samson snapped them like a burnt thread.
stages.prompt: When Delilah first asked, what did Samson say would make him weak?
options: Being bound with chains of iron
Having his eyes put out
Being bound with seven green withs that were never dried
Being kept from eating bread and drinking water
stages.explanation: Samson told Delilah, "If they bind me with seven green withs that were never dried, then shall I be weak" (Judges 16:7), yet he broke them when she bound him (Judges 16:9).
stages.hint: Look for something freshly cut that had not yet dried out.

stages.clue: Witness statement: "She pressed him daily with her words, until his soul was vexed unto death. Then he finally told her all his heart."
stages.prompt: What secret did Samson finally reveal to Delilah?
options: That his strength came from a hidden amulet he wore
That no razor had come upon his head, for he had been a Nazarite unto God from his mother's womb
That he would lose his strength if he ever drank wine
That he could be weakened only if he were bound while asleep
stages.explanation: In Judges 16:17 Samson said, "There hath not come a razor upon mine head; for I have been a Nazarite unto God from my mother's womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me."
stages.hint: The secret concerns his head and a lifelong vow to God.

stages.clue: Final report: Samson awoke and said he would go out as at other times, but this time the Philistines took him. The text adds that he did not know something had changed.
stages.prompt: What really happened that left Samson powerless?
options: Delilah bound him with new ropes while the Philistines held him down
He was wounded in battle and carried to Gaza
While he slept upon Delilah's knees, a man shaved off the seven locks of his head, and his strength went from him
The lords of the Philistines put out his eyes before he could escape
stages.explanation: Judges 16:19 says Delilah "made him sleep upon her knees" and had a man "shave off the seven locks of his head," and "his strength went from him"; verse 20 adds that "he wist not that the LORD was departed from him."
stages.hint: Remember the secret he revealed in the previous stage, and what happened while he slept.

briefing: In 1 Kings 3, two women stand before King Solomon with one living baby and one dead one, and each claims the living child as her own. There were no other witnesses in the house, so the king must uncover the truth from their testimony alone. Gather the evidence and discover how the true mother was revealed.

stages.clue: Court record: two women arrived together and stood before the king. The first testified that they shared a home and that she had given birth there.
stages.prompt: According to the first woman, what was the living arrangement of the two women?
options: They dwelt together in one house
They lived in separate cities
They lived in the king's palace
They were traveling strangers who met at an inn
stages.explanation: The first woman said, "I and this woman dwell in one house; and I was delivered of a child with her in the house" (1 Kings 3:17).
stages.hint: Listen to how she describes where they both live.

stages.clue: Witness statement: the second baby was born three days after the first, and no stranger was with them in the house. One of the infants did not survive the night.
stages.prompt: According to the testimony, how did the other woman's child die?
options: It fell sick with a fever
She overlaid it in the night
It was taken by a stranger
It died at birth
stages.explanation: The first woman testified, "this woman's child died in the night; because she overlaid it" (1 Kings 3:19).
stages.hint: The cause happened while the mother lay with the child at night.

stages.clue: Witness statement: "She arose at midnight... while thine handmaid slept." At morning, the first woman examined the dead child closely.
stages.prompt: What did the first woman claim happened at midnight?
options: The other woman fled the house with both babies
A servant switched the children
The other woman took her son and laid her dead child in her bosom
She woke and found both babies missing
stages.explanation: She said the other woman "took my son from beside me... and laid her dead child in my bosom," and in the morning she saw "it was not my son, which I did bear" (1 Kings 3:20-21).
stages.hint: Think about what was exchanged while she slept.

stages.clue: Evidence log: after hearing both women insist the living child was theirs, the king called for an unusual object, and it was brought before him.
stages.prompt: What did the king command after the sword was brought?
options: That both women be sent away
That the living child be divided in two, half to each woman
That the child be given to the elders of the city
That the women draw lots for the child
stages.explanation: The king said, "Bring me a sword," and then, "Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other" (1 Kings 3:24-25).
stages.hint: He asked for a sword; consider what he ordered next.

stages.clue: Final testimony: one woman's "bowels yearned upon her son" and she spoke up at once; the other woman answered very differently. The king then gave his verdict.
stages.prompt: Whom did the king declare to be the true mother of the living child?
options: The woman who said, "Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it"
Neither woman, so the king kept the child
Both women, who were told to share the child
The woman who pleaded, "Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it"
stages.explanation: The woman whose bowels yearned for her son begged that the child be given away rather than slain, and the king said, "Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof" (1 Kings 3:26-27).
stages.hint: Which woman was willing to give up her claim so the child would live?

briefing: Two strangers from the camp of Israel slipped into Jericho, and by nightfall the king's men were knocking at a house on the town wall. Your case file is Joshua 2: follow the evidence in story order to learn who sent the men, where they vanished, and how they escaped the city.

stages.clue: Camp record: two men departed from Shittim under orders to view the land, even Jericho. They were later traced to the house of a woman named Rahab.
stages.prompt: According to the record, who sent the two men out to spy?
options: Joshua the son of Nun
The king of Jericho
Moses the servant of the LORD
Rahab
stages.explanation: Joshua 2:1 states that Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho.
stages.hint: Look for the leader named at the very start of the chapter, identified by his father's name.

stages.clue: Statement given to the king's messengers: 'There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were... pursue after them quickly.' Yet the searchers found no one in the house.
stages.prompt: Where were the two men actually hidden?
options: On the roof, under stalks of flax
In a cave outside the city
In the king's own storehouse
At the bottom of a well
stages.explanation: Joshua 2:6 says she had brought them up to the roof of the house and hid them with the stalks of flax which she had laid in order upon the roof.
stages.hint: Think high, not low, and of something she had laid out in order there.

stages.clue: Gatekeeper's report: the king's men rode out after the spies, and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the city gate was shut behind them.
stages.prompt: Which way did the pursuers go in search of the men?
options: The way to Jordan unto the fords
Toward the Red sea
Back to Shittim
North to the mountain of Lebanon
stages.explanation: Joshua 2:7 records that the men pursued after them the way to Jordan unto the fords, and the gate was shut once they had gone out.
stages.hint: The pursuers headed toward a river crossing.

stages.clue: Overheard on the roof before the men lay down: the woman spoke of what Jericho had heard about the Red sea and about the kings Sihon and Og.
stages.prompt: What did Rahab tell the spies she knew?
options: That the LORD had given them the land
That the king of Jericho would make peace with Israel
That Jericho's walls could never be taken
That the spies had been seen at Shittim
stages.explanation: In Joshua 2:9 Rahab says, I know that the LORD hath given you the land, and in verse 11 she confesses that the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.
stages.hint: Her words began with 'I know' and concerned who would possess the land.

stages.clue: Final evidence: her house was upon the town wall. The spies told her to gather her household and to bind a token in the very window they had used; she answered, 'According unto your words, so be it.'
stages.prompt: What really happened: how did the spies leave Jericho, and what marked Rahab's house?
options: She let them down by a cord through the window, and she bound a scarlet line in that window
They walked out through the city gate at dawn, and she painted the door with blood
They hid in a cart of flax, and she hung a white cloth on her roof
They climbed down a ladder, and she placed a lamp in the window
stages.explanation: Joshua 2:15 says she let them down by a cord through the window because her house was upon the town wall, and Joshua 2:21 says she bound the scarlet line in the window.
stages.hint: Remember where her house stood, and the color of the thread the spies named.

briefing: Jacob has left Paddan-aram with his wives, children and flocks, and Laban has discovered that his household images are gone. Working only from Genesis 31, piece together when they vanished, how Laban gave chase, what was said, and where the missing gods really were.

stages.clue: Shepherd's log: the master of the house was away from his tents tending to the flock when the images vanished, and Jacob left without telling him.
stages.prompt: According to the text, what was Laban doing when the images were taken?
options: He had gone to shear his sheep
He was offering a sacrifice on mount Gilead
He was at a wedding feast in Haran
He was digging a well in Gerar
stages.explanation: Genesis 31:19 says Laban went to shear his sheep, and while he was away the images that were his were stolen. Jacob then fled over the river toward mount Gilead (Genesis 31:21).
stages.hint: Think about seasonal work with a flock.

stages.clue: Messenger's report: word of Jacob's flight reached Laban late, and he set out with his brethren on a long pursuit.
stages.prompt: Where did Laban and his brethren overtake Jacob?
options: At the brook Jabbok
In the mount Gilead
At the well of Bethel
At the gates of Shechem
stages.explanation: Laban was told on the third day that Jacob had fled, pursued him seven days' journey, and overtook him in the mount Gilead (Genesis 31:22-23).
stages.hint: It is the same place Jacob had set his face toward when he fled.

stages.clue: Witness statement from the confrontation: Laban questioned why Jacob left, then made a pointed accusation about his gods; Jacob answered with a grave pledge.
stages.prompt: What did Jacob say should happen to whoever was found with Laban's gods?
options: He should pay double to Laban
He should be sent back to Haran
He should not live
He should serve Laban seven years
stages.explanation: When Laban asked why Jacob had stolen his gods, Jacob said, "With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live" (Genesis 31:32). The text adds that Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.
stages.hint: Jacob's pledge was far more severe than a fine or a period of service.

stages.clue: Search record: Laban went from tent to tent through the camp, finding nothing in the first several he entered.
stages.prompt: Which tent did Laban enter after leaving Leah's tent?
options: Jacob's tent
The two maidservants' tents
Rachel's tent
Laban's own tent
stages.explanation: Laban searched Jacob's tent, Leah's tent and the two maidservants' tents without finding the gods, then went out of Leah's tent and entered into Rachel's tent (Genesis 31:33).
stages.hint: One wife's tent had not yet been searched.

stages.clue: Final detail: Laban searched the entire last tent, yet its occupant stayed seated and asked him not to be displeased that she could not rise.
stages.prompt: Case solved: where were the missing images during the search?
options: Buried under the floor of Jacob's tent
Hidden among the flocks by the maidservants
Placed in the camel's furniture, with Rachel sitting upon them
Carried ahead across the river by Leah's sons
stages.explanation: Rachel had taken the images, put them in the camel's furniture, and sat upon them, so Laban searched but found them not (Genesis 31:34-35).
stages.hint: The person who stayed seated during the search is the key.

briefing: A grieving father in Canaan holds a torn, blood-soaked garment and believes his favoured son is dead. Your assignment is to trace the coat's journey from Jacob's tent to the wilderness pit and uncover what really happened, using only the testimony of Genesis 37.

stages.clue: Evidence item #1: A richly made garment, unlike anything the other brothers wear. Witnesses say the father gave it to only one son.
stages.prompt: According to the text, why did Israel love Joseph more than all his children and make him this coat?
options: Because Joseph was the son of his old age
Because Joseph was the firstborn son
Because Joseph had saved the family flocks
Because Joseph had been chosen by the elders
stages.explanation: Genesis 37:3 says Israel loved Joseph more than all his children 'because he was the son of his old age: and he made him a coat of many colours.' Genesis 37:4 adds that his brothers hated him for this favour.
stages.hint: Think about Joseph's age compared with his father's age when he was born.

stages.clue: Witness statement from a brother: 'He told us his dream about the field, and we hated him yet the more.'
stages.prompt: In Joseph's first dream, what made obeisance to his sheaf?
options: The sun, the moon, and eleven stars
His brothers' sheaves
Seven fat kine
The flocks of his father
stages.explanation: In Genesis 37:7 Joseph says his sheaf stood upright and 'your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.' Genesis 37:8 says the brothers hated him yet the more for his dreams and his words.
stages.hint: The brothers were binding something in the field when the dream began.

stages.clue: Travel log: Joseph was sent from the vale of Hebron to check on his brothers, but they were not where he expected. A stranger in the field redirected him.
stages.prompt: Where did Joseph finally find his brothers?
options: In Shechem
In Bethel
In Dothan
In Beersheba
stages.explanation: Joseph went to Shechem, but a man told him, 'I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan.' Genesis 37:17 says Joseph 'found them in Dothan.'
stages.hint: His first destination was not his final one; follow the stranger's directions.

stages.clue: Scene report: The coat was stripped from its owner near an empty hole in the wilderness. One brother had urged, 'Shed no blood.'
stages.prompt: Which brother proposed casting Joseph into the pit instead of killing him?
options: Judah
Simeon
Levi
Reuben
stages.explanation: Genesis 37:22 records Reuben saying, 'Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness,' intending to deliver him to his father. Verse 24 notes the pit was empty, with no water in it.
stages.hint: This brother hoped to rescue Joseph and return him to his father.

stages.clue: The father's verdict upon seeing the coat: 'It is my son's coat; an evil beast hath devoured him.' But the blood on the coat tells a different story.
stages.prompt: What really happened to Joseph and the coat?
options: An evil beast killed Joseph in the field and tore his coat
Joseph was sold for twenty pieces of silver, and his brothers dipped his coat in the blood of a kid of the goats
Reuben slew Joseph secretly and hid the coat in the pit
The Ishmeelites killed Joseph and left the coat in Dothan
stages.explanation: Genesis 37:28 says Joseph was lifted out of the pit and sold to the Ishmeelites 'for twenty pieces of silver,' and verse 31 says the brothers 'killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood.' Jacob, deceived, concluded in verse 33 that a beast had devoured him.
stages.hint: Whose blood was really on the coat? Judah asked what profit there was in slaying their brother.

briefing: After the stunning fall of Jericho, Israel suffers an unexpected and humiliating defeat at the small city of Ai. Something has gone terribly wrong in the camp, and the LORD reveals that a hidden wrong must be uncovered before Israel can stand again. Investigate the case of 'The Hidden Plunder' in Joshua 7.

stages.clue: Field report from Ai: About three thousand men went up confidently, yet they returned in retreat, and the hearts of the people melted like water.
stages.prompt: What happened to the Israelite force that went up against Ai?
options: They fled before the men of Ai, who smote about thirty and six of them
They captured Ai without losing a single man
They besieged Ai for seven days until its walls fell
They made a peace treaty with the king of Ai
keywords: fled before the men of Ai
stages.explanation: About three thousand men went up, but they fled before the men of Ai, who smote about thirty and six of them, and the people's hearts melted (Joshua 7:4-5).
stages.hint: The report speaks of retreat and casualties, not victory.

stages.clue: Statement from the LORD to Joshua, who lay on his face before the ark: 'Get thee up; wherefore liest thou thus upon thy face?'
stages.prompt: According to the LORD, why could Israel not stand before their enemies?
options: Israel had taken of the accursed thing, stolen, dissembled, and put it among their own stuff
Israel had made a golden calf at the foot of the mountain
Israel had made a covenant with the Gibeonites
Israel had sent too few soldiers against Ai
stages.explanation: The LORD said Israel had sinned, taking of the accursed thing, stealing, dissembling, and putting it among their own stuff, therefore they could not stand before their enemies (Joshua 7:11-12).
stages.hint: The problem was something hidden inside the camp, not a lack of soldiers.

stages.clue: Instruction for the morning: the people are to sanctify themselves, for there is an accursed thing in the midst of Israel.
stages.prompt: How did the LORD say the guilty person would be identified?
options: The people would be brought by tribes, then families, then households, then man by man, as the LORD took them
Each man would be asked to swear an oath before the priests
The elders would search every tent in the camp at night
The guilty one would be struck with leprosy
stages.explanation: The LORD commanded that Israel be brought according to their tribes, and the one taken would come by families, then households, then man by man (Joshua 7:14).
stages.hint: Think of a narrowing process, from the largest group down to the individual.

stages.clue: Early morning record: Joshua rose up early and brought Israel by their tribes, narrowing the search step by step.
stages.prompt: Which tribe and family were taken as the search narrowed?
options: The tribe of Judah and the family of the Zarhites
The tribe of Benjamin and the family of the Matrites
The tribe of Levi and the family of the Kohathites
The tribe of Ephraim and the family of the Shuthelahites
stages.explanation: The tribe of Judah was taken, then the family of the Zarhites, and then Zabdi was taken (Joshua 7:16-17).
stages.hint: This tribe would later be known as the tribe of King David.

stages.clue: Confession recorded before Joshua: 'When I saw among the spoils... then I coveted them, and took them.'
stages.prompt: Case solved: who took the hidden plunder, and what did he take?
options: Achan son of Carmi, who took a goodly Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight
Zabdi, who took the golden vessels of the house of the LORD
Joshua's servant, who took the crown of the king of Jericho
Carmi, who took cattle and sheep from the spoil of Ai
stages.explanation: Achan son of Carmi was taken, and he confessed that he coveted and took a Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold, hiding them in the earth in his tent (Joshua 7:18, 21).
stages.hint: The man taken was the grandson of the one taken in the previous stage.

briefing: In the early Jerusalem church, a couple sold a possession and brought money to the apostles, but within hours both were dead and fear had spread through the whole church. Your case file covers Acts 5:1-11. Follow the money, the words spoken, and the timeline to learn what really happened with the price of the land.

stages.clue: Ledger note: A man and his wife sold a possession. Only part of the money ever reached the apostles' feet, and the wife was aware of it.
stages.prompt: According to the text, what did Ananias do with the money from the sale?
options: He kept back part of the price and laid a certain part at the apostles' feet
He gave the entire price to the poor in the streets
He refused to sell the possession at all
He gave the whole price to Sapphira to manage
keywords: kept back part of the price
stages.explanation: Acts 5:1-2 says Ananias, with Sapphira, sold a possession, kept back part of the price with his wife being privy to it, and laid a certain part at the apostles' feet.
stages.hint: Look at how much of the price actually arrived at the apostles' feet.

stages.clue: Witness statement (Peter): 'Whiles it remained, was it not thine own?' The questioning then turns to whom the lie was really told.
stages.prompt: According to Peter, what was true about the land and the money, and to whom had Ananias lied?
options: The land belonged to the apostles, and he lied to the elders
The land and money were his own and in his power, and he lied not unto men but unto God
He was required to give everything, and he lied only to his wife
The money belonged to the temple, and he lied to the priests
keywords: lied unto men, but unto God
stages.explanation: In Acts 5:3-4 Peter says the land was Ananias's own and the price was in his own power, yet he had lied to the Holy Ghost: 'thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.'
stages.hint: Peter asks two questions about ownership before naming the one who was lied to.

stages.clue: Coroner's note: The first subject collapsed immediately upon hearing Peter's words. Certain men of the congregation handled the burial.
stages.prompt: What happened to Ananias after he heard Peter's words?
options: He repented and was restored to the church
He fled the city before anyone could stop him
He fell down and gave up the ghost, and the young men carried him out and buried him
He was put in prison by the council
stages.explanation: Acts 5:5-6 records that Ananias fell down and gave up the ghost, great fear came on all who heard, and the young men wound him up, carried him out, and buried him.
stages.hint: Notice both what happened to him and who arose afterward.

stages.clue: Timeline entry: Some hours later the wife entered, unaware of what had happened. Peter asked her a single question about the sale price.
stages.prompt: How did Sapphira answer when Peter asked whether they sold the land for so much?
options: She said she did not know the price
She confessed that they had kept back part
She said her husband had sold it without her knowledge
She said, 'Yea, for so much'
stages.explanation: Acts 5:7-8 says that about three hours later Sapphira, not knowing what was done, came in, and when Peter asked about the price she answered, 'Yea, for so much.'
stages.hint: Her answer echoes Peter's own words back to him.

stages.clue: Final report: Peter told her the feet of those who buried her husband were at the door. Afterward the whole church was affected.
stages.prompt: Solution: What does the text say really happened with Ananias and Sapphira?
options: They had agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord; she also fell down dead and was buried by her husband, and great fear came upon all the church
Sapphira alone planned the deception, and Ananias knew nothing of it
The apostles wrongly accused them, and the church was ashamed
They returned the hidden money, and the matter was quietly settled
stages.explanation: In Acts 5:9-11 Peter asks how they had agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord; Sapphira fell down and yielded up the ghost, was buried by her husband, and great fear came upon all the church.
stages.hint: Peter's question shows whether the couple acted alone or jointly.

briefing: During a royal banquet in Babylon, a disembodied hand writes a message on the palace wall, and the king's wise men cannot explain it. Your task is to work through the case file in Daniel 5 and find out what the writing meant and what happened that same night.

stages.clue: Evidence from the banquet hall: a thousand lords drinking wine from golden and silver cups. A servant reports that these cups were not originally made for the palace.
stages.prompt: According to the record, where had the vessels used at Belshazzar's feast come from?
options: The temple of the house of God at Jerusalem, taken by Nebuchadnezzar
The treasury of the Medes and Persians, received as tribute
The royal workshops of Babylon, made for this feast
The temple of Bel, brought in by the Chaldean priests
stages.explanation: Belshazzar ordered the golden and silver vessels that his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple in Jerusalem, and the guests drank from them while praising gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood and stone (Daniel 5:1-4).
stages.hint: The text names the city these cups were taken from and the king who took them.

stages.clue: Witness statement: 'The king saw it near the candlestick. His face changed, and his knees knocked together.'
stages.prompt: What did the king see appear in the palace that same hour?
options: Fingers of a man's hand writing upon the plaister of the wall
An angel standing beside the candlestick with a drawn sword
A burning scroll that fell onto the king's table
A voice from heaven that spoke the words aloud to all the lords
stages.explanation: Fingers of a man's hand came forth and wrote over against the candlestick on the plaister of the palace wall, and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote and was badly shaken (Daniel 5:5-6).
stages.hint: The king saw only part of something, and it was writing.

stages.clue: The king's astrologers and soothsayers have failed to read the writing. Then someone enters the banquet house with a recommendation.
stages.prompt: Who came into the banquet house and told the king about a man in whom was 'the spirit of the holy gods'?
options: The queen
The chief of the astrologers
Darius the Median
One of the king's concubines
stages.explanation: The queen came into the banquet house, recalled how Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, had shown light, understanding and wisdom, and advised that he be called to give the interpretation (Daniel 5:10-12).
stages.hint: This person came in because of the king's and his lords' words, and remembered Daniel from Nebuchadnezzar's days.

stages.clue: Daniel turns down the king's gifts, then recounts what happened to Nebuchadnezzar before he addresses Belshazzar directly.
stages.prompt: What charge did Daniel bring against Belshazzar?
options: He had not humbled his heart, though he knew all this, but had lifted himself up against the Lord of heaven
He had broken a treaty with the Medes and Persians
He had refused to pay the wise men of Babylon for their service
He had thrown Daniel's friends into a fiery furnace
stages.explanation: Daniel said Belshazzar had not humbled his heart, though he knew all this, but had lifted himself up against the Lord of heaven by drinking from His vessels and praising idols while not glorifying the God who held his breath (Daniel 5:22-23).
stages.hint: Consider what Belshazzar did with the vessels and whom he praised.

stages.clue: The final report reads MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN. A note at the bottom of the file adds: 'In that night...'
stages.prompt: Case solved: what did the writing announce, and what really happened?
options: The king was weighed in the balances and found wanting; that night Belshazzar was slain and Darius the Median took the kingdom
The king would reign forty more years if he repented; he did, and Babylon was spared
The kingdom would be divided among Belshazzar's sons; Daniel was made king
The wise men would be destroyed; Belshazzar had them executed the next morning
stages.explanation: Daniel interpreted the writing: the kingdom was numbered and finished, the king was weighed in the balances and found wanting, and the kingdom was divided and given to the Medes and Persians. In that night Belshazzar was slain, and Darius the Median took the kingdom (Daniel 5:25-31).
stages.hint: TEKEL concerns a measurement, and the fulfilment came very quickly.

briefing: On the night of the Passover, Jesus sat at the table with his twelve disciples and announced that one of them would betray him. Using the accounts in Matthew 26 and John 13, trace how the agreement was made, how the betrayer was revealed at the table, and what sign was finally used to deliver Jesus over.

stages.clue: A record from the chief priests' meeting: one of the twelve came asking, 'What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you?' A sum was agreed upon.
stages.prompt: For what price did Judas Iscariot covenant with the chief priests?
options: Thirty pieces of silver
Fifty shekels of gold
A field outside Jerusalem
Three hundred pence
stages.explanation: Judas went to the chief priests and 'they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver,' after which he sought opportunity to betray Jesus (Matthew 26:14-16).
stages.hint: The payment was counted out in coins of a common metal, not gold.

stages.clue: Witness statement from the table: 'As we were eating, the Master said one of us would betray him. We were exceeding sorrowful, and each began to ask him a question.'
stages.prompt: When Judas asked, 'Master, is it I?', how did Jesus answer him?
options: "Thou hast said."
"Not thou, but another."
"Ask Peter."
He gave no answer at all.
stages.explanation: When Judas, 'which betrayed him,' asked 'Master, is it I?', Jesus replied, 'Thou hast said' (Matthew 26:25).
stages.hint: Jesus answered with a brief phrase that turned Judas's own words back to him.

stages.clue: Seating detail: the disciple whom Jesus loved was leaning on Jesus' bosom. Simon Peter beckoned to him to ask who the betrayer was.
stages.prompt: What sign did Jesus say would identify the one who would betray him?
options: The one to whom he would give a sop after dipping it
The one who would leave the room first
The one who refused to have his feet washed
The one sitting at his right hand
stages.explanation: Jesus said, 'He it is, to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it,' and he gave the sop to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon (John 13:26).
stages.hint: Watch what Jesus handed across the table.

stages.clue: After Jesus told Judas, 'That thou doest, do quickly,' none at the table understood the remark. Judas went out immediately.
stages.prompt: Why did some of the disciples think Judas was leaving?
options: Because he had the bag, they thought he was sent to buy things for the feast or give to the poor
They thought he was going to fetch more wine for the table
They thought he was going to prepare the upper room
They thought he was going to bring Mary and Martha
stages.explanation: Some thought, 'because Judas had the bag,' that Jesus had told him to buy what was needed for the feast or to give something to the poor; Judas went out, 'and it was night' (John 13:29-30).
stages.hint: Consider what Judas was responsible for carrying among the disciples.

stages.clue: Garden report: a great multitude with swords and staves arrived from the chief priests and elders. Their guide had arranged a signal beforehand so they would seize the right man.
stages.prompt: Case solved: what sign did Judas use to deliver Jesus to the multitude?
options: He greeted Jesus with 'Hail, master' and kissed him
He pointed at Jesus and called out his name
He placed the thirty pieces of silver at Jesus' feet
He embraced Peter so the soldiers would know the group
stages.explanation: Judas had told them, 'Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast,' and he came to Jesus, said 'Hail, master; and kissed him' (Matthew 26:48-49).
stages.hint: The signal was a greeting normally given as a sign of friendship.

briefing: Case file: The Prisoner Who Walked Free. Peter has been locked in a heavily guarded prison by King Herod, yet by morning he is gone and the soldiers cannot account for him. Investigate the evidence recorded in Acts 12 to discover how the prisoner walked free.

stages.clue: Court record: King Herod has already killed James the brother of John with the sword. Shortly afterward, during the days of unleavened bread, he orders a second arrest.
stages.prompt: According to the record, why did Herod proceed to take Peter as well?
options: Because he saw it pleased the Jews
Because Peter had insulted him in the temple
Because the Roman governor ordered it
Because Peter had tried to free James
stages.explanation: Acts 12:3 states that because Herod saw that killing James pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. He then imprisoned him under four quaternions of soldiers (Acts 12:4).
stages.hint: Look at Herod's reaction to how people responded to the death of James.

stages.clue: Guard report: On the night before Herod planned to bring the prisoner out, the cell was under full watch, with keepers stationed before the door.
stages.prompt: How was Peter being held that night?
options: Sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains
Alone in a pit sealed with a stone
Standing in stocks in the inner prison
Locked in a tower with no guards inside
stages.explanation: Acts 12:6 records that Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, while keepers before the door kept the prison. Meanwhile, Acts 12:5 notes the church prayed without ceasing for him.
stages.hint: The record mentions a pair of soldiers and a pair of restraints.

stages.clue: Scene evidence: Witnesses inside the prison would have seen a light shine in the cell. Peter's chains were found fallen from his hands, and he passed the first and second ward.
stages.prompt: What happened when Peter and his escort reached the iron gate leading to the city?
options: It opened to them of his own accord
Peter broke the lock with his chains
A sympathetic guard unlocked it
They climbed over it with a rope
stages.explanation: Acts 12:10 says the iron gate that leads to the city opened to them of his own accord. Then they passed through one street, and the angel departed from Peter.
stages.hint: No human hand is mentioned at the gate.

stages.clue: Witness statement: A young woman at a house where many were gathered praying heard a familiar voice knocking at the gate, but she ran inside instead of opening it.
stages.prompt: Who was this witness, and at whose house did it happen?
options: Rhoda, at the house of Mary the mother of John Mark
Lydia, at the house of Simon the tanner
Dorcas, at the house of Cornelius
Priscilla, at the house of Jason
stages.explanation: Acts 12:12-13 identifies the house of Mary the mother of John whose surname was Mark, and the damsel named Rhoda. For gladness she did not open the gate but ran in to tell that Peter stood there (Acts 12:14).
stages.hint: The house belonged to the mother of a man whose surname was Mark.

stages.clue: Final testimony: Once inside, Peter beckoned the astonished gathering to hold their peace and gave his own account before departing to another place.
stages.prompt: Case solution: according to Peter's own declaration, how did he get out of prison?
options: The Lord had brought him out of the prison
Herod quietly released him to avoid a riot
The church members bribed the keepers
He slipped his chains and escaped by his own strength
keywords: brought him out of the prison
stages.explanation: Acts 12:17 records that Peter declared to them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. He then told them to show these things to James and to the brethren.
stages.hint: Peter credits neither himself nor any human helper.

briefing: In the court of king Ahasuerus at Shushan, a royal decree has gone out to destroy every Jew in the empire on a single appointed day, and the queen herself is secretly one of the people marked for death. Investigate Esther 3-7 to trace who set the plot in motion, how it was arranged, and how it was finally exposed.

stages.clue: Witness statement from the king's servants at the gate: 'All of us bowed to the newly promoted official as the king commanded, but one man refused day after day. He had told us he was a Jew.'
stages.prompt: According to the text, what did Haman seek to do after learning that Mordecai would not bow to him?
options: Destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom
Have Mordecai alone quietly removed from the king's gate
Petition the king to promote Mordecai in his place
Banish Mordecai and his household from Shushan
stages.explanation: When Mordecai 'bowed not, nor did him reverence,' Haman was 'full of wrath' and 'sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus' (Esther 3:2-6).
stages.hint: Haman thought scorn to lay hands on just one man.

stages.clue: Recovered from Haman's chambers: a record that in the month Nisan a lot was cast before him day to day and month to month until it settled on a particular month.
stages.prompt: To which month did the lot, called Pur, fall for carrying out the plot?
options: The first month, Nisan
The third month, Sivan
The twelfth month, Adar
The seventh month, Tisri
stages.explanation: They cast 'Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, to the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar' (Esther 3:7).
stages.hint: The lot was cast in the first month but ran on until the last month of the year.

stages.clue: Message carried by Hatach from the queen to Mordecai: 'Whosoever shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, there is one law of his to put him to death.'
stages.prompt: How long did Esther say it had been since she was called to come in unto the king?
options: Seven days
Thirty days
Three days
Twelve months
stages.explanation: Esther explained that only those to whom the king held out 'the golden sceptre' would live, and 'I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days' (Esther 4:11).
stages.hint: The number Esther gives is longer than the fast she later calls for.

stages.clue: Overheard at Haman's house after the queen's banquet: his wife and friends urged him to have a structure built before morning so he could ask the king about Mordecai.
stages.prompt: How high did Zeresh and Haman's friends say the gallows should be made?
options: Twenty cubits
A hundred cubits
Thirty cubits
Fifty cubits
stages.explanation: Zeresh his wife and all his friends said, 'Let a gallows be made of fifty cubits high,' and 'he caused the gallows to be made' (Esther 5:14).
stages.hint: The same figure appears again when a chamberlain points out the gallows in Haman's house.

stages.clue: At the second banquet the queen begs for her life and her people's, saying they are sold to be destroyed. The king demands to know who durst presume in his heart to do so.
stages.prompt: Whom did Esther name as the adversary, and what became of him?
options: Mordecai, who was sent away from the king's gate
Haman, who was hanged on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai
Harbonah, who was removed from the king's chamberlains
Bigthan, who was hanged for conspiring against the king
stages.explanation: Esther said, 'The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman,' and 'they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai' (Esther 7:6, 10).
stages.hint: The man who built the gallows met it himself.

batch.title: The Plot Against the Queen's People
